category: MEGA command-line client (public-link downloader and account client)

free_tier.stated: 'Megatools is a collection of programs for accessing Mega service from a command line of your desktop or server.' Free software; the command set includes 'dl Download file from a "public" Mega link (doesn't require login)'.
free_tier.notes: The project site megatools.megous.com answered HTTP 503 'We'll be back soon' (scheduled maintenance) today, so the man page was read from a mirror of the same document.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: MEGA states it has no file size limit; the local disk is the cap.

retention.stated: not applicable: writes to local disk; no service-side storage.

egress.terms: MEGA's IP-based six-hour transfer window applies to the machine running megatools; there is no megatools-side quota or proxy rotation.

interface_detail: Subcommands: df, ls, get, put, copy, rm, mkdir, export, reg, test and 'dl' for public links. Streaming is supported with '--path -', so a wrapper can pipe a public link into another process without touching disk.
tooling: Native builds for Windows and Linux, plus source. A shell wrapper is enough; nothing needs a GUI or a display.
chaining: The streaming flag makes it the cheapest MEGA leg for a pipeline that must not stage the file on local disk: piped output can go straight into an uploader or a hash check.

limits.value: MEGA counts downloads from the IP over six hours; no fixed number published

limits_note: MEGA's help page lists third-party tools as a hazard: 'these tools can't detect your quota', and using them with account credentials can lock the account. Public-link download avoids the credential risk.
binding_note: The six-hour per-IP window is the only quota in the path; megatools does not rotate proxies, so the client meets it directly and must wait for the reset.

identity_cost.detail: 'megatools dl' takes a public link and needs no login. Account subcommands exist for private files but are not required for the public-link path.

reliability_note: The project site was 503 today and the man page had to be read from a mirror; the tool is maintained but the distribution site is not always up. Over-quota downloads fail mid-transfer and resume after the window resets.
confidence_note: Man page and MEGA quota page read; the project site's 503 is measured. Running 'megatools dl' against a real link would raise this to measured.

evidence.proved: 'dl Download file from a "public" Mega link (doesn't require login)'; streaming with 'megatools get --path -'
the project site is down for maintenance: HTTP 503, 17 words, 'This site is currently undergoing scheduled maintenance.'
per-IP six-hour download limit for free and anonymous users; no fixed limit
third-party tools 'can't detect your quota' and may cause account lock-ups when given credentials

notes: Tooling note applies: a CLI is not a hosted path, but this one is a single binary and a one-line wrapper, and it streams, so it is the least-bad local MEGA leg. It does not satisfy 'no install'.
